Source: step 1 of the supplied proof of the parent theorem intcpt_flat_limit_integer_multiplicity (case n = 0: the weights are sums of integer point masses, μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)) → θ₀, so θ₀ ∈ ℕ); the last step uses closedness of ℕ in ℝ instead of eventual constancy. Notation: G := Grassmannian N 0; H^0 := μHE[0]; μ_V := V.weight = V.measure.map Prod.fst; B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ, B°_ρ(y) := ball y ρ; v(T) := planeVarifoldMeasure T = (H^0⌞T.plane).map (y ↦ (y,T)). (H) denotes the hypothesis ∫ f dW_k → θ₀ ∫ f dv(P) for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ) with tsupport f ⊆ B°_5(0) × G.
1. dim P.plane = 0 (Grassmannian.finrank_plane), so P.plane = ⊥ (Submodule.finrank_eq_zero) and P.plane = {0} as a set.
2. H^0 = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and μH[0]{x} = 1 for every x (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Consequently ∫_{P.plane} g dH^0 = ∫_{{0}} g dH^0 = H^0{0}·g(0) = g(0) for every g (integral_singleton).
3. Claim: for every k, μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)).toReal is a natural number (μ_k := μ_{W_k}).
  3a. IsIntegral W_k gives M, θ with IsVarifoldOf W_k M θ and θ ∈ ℕ for (H^0⌞M)-a.e. point.
  3b. M is countable: CountablyRectifiable 0 M gives M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j with H^0(M₀) = 0 and F_j : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 0) → ℝ^N. M₀ = ∅ because any x ∈ M₀ would give 1 = H^0{x} ≤ H^0(M₀) = 0. The domain of F_j is a subsingleton, so range F_j = {F_j(0)}. Hence M ⊆ ⋃_j {F_j(0)} is countable.
  3c. θ(x) ∈ ℕ for every x ∈ M: with Bad := {x : θ(x) ∉ ℕ}, H^0(Bad ∩ M) ≤ (H^0⌞M)(Bad) = 0 (Measure.le_restrict_apply and the a.e. statement), and a point of Bad ∩ M would have H^0-measure 1 ≤ 0.
  3d. B := B_{1/2}(0) is Borel. μ_k(B) = W_k.measure(B × G) (Varifold.weight_apply) = ∫⁻_S ofReal θ dH^0 by IsVarifoldOf, where S := {x ∈ M : ∃ S', (weighted approximate tangent at x) ∧ (x,S') ∈ B × G} ⊆ M is countable. By lintegral_countable, this equals Σ'_{x∈S} ofReal θ(x)·H^0{x} = Σ'_{x∈S} (⌊θ(x)⌋₊ : [0,∞]) (θ(x) is a natural number by 3c, so ofReal θ(x) = ⌊θ(x)⌋₊).
  3e. If this sum is ∞, its toReal is 0 ∈ ℕ. Otherwise only finitely many x ∈ S have ⌊θ(x)⌋₊ ≥ 1 (ENNReal.finite_const_le_of_tsum_ne_top with ε = 1) and all other terms are 0, so the sum equals the finite sum Σ ⌊θ(x)⌋₊ over that finite set (tsum_eq_sum), the cast of a natural number; its toReal is that natural number.
4. Cutoffs. g₁(x) := max(0, min(1, 2 − 4|x|)) and g₂(x) := max(0, min(1, 3 − 4|x|)) are continuous and [0,1]-valued; g₁ = 0 for |x| ≥ 1/2, g₂ = 1 for |x| ≤ 1/2, both vanish for |x| ≥ 3/4 (so tsupport g_i ⊆ B_{3/4}(0), which is compact and contained in B°_5(0)), and g₁(0) = g₂(0) = 1.
5. By the sibling weight_tendsto and 2, ∫ g_i dμ_k → θ₀∫_{P.plane} g_i dH^0 = θ₀g_i(0) = θ₀ (i = 1, 2).
6. μ_k(B_{3/4}(0)) < ∞ (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact), and |g_i| ≤ 1 vanishes off B_{3/4}(0), so g_i is μ_k-integrable. Since g₁ ≤ 1_{B_{1/2}(0)} ≤ g₂ pointwise: ofReal(∫ g₁ dμ_k) = ∫⁻ ofReal g₁ dμ_k ≤ μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)) ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal g₂ dμ_k = ofReal(∫ g₂ dμ_k) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, lintegral_indicator_one, lintegral_mono).
7. By 5, 6, continuity of ofReal and the squeeze theorem, μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)) → ofReal θ₀ in [0,∞]. As ofReal θ₀ ≠ ∞, toReal is continuous there (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), so μ_k(B_{1/2}(0)).toReal → (ofReal θ₀).toReal = θ₀ (θ₀ ≥ 0).
8. The range of ℕ → ℝ is closed (Nat.isClosedEmbedding_coe_real). By 3 every term of the real sequence in 7 lies in it, so its limit θ₀ lies in it (IsClosed.mem_of_tendsto): θ₀ = m for some m ∈ ℕ.
